title: '…()' directly created in 'with' has no effect.
summary: Used when a new lock instance is created by using with statement which has no effect. Instead, an existing instance should be used to acquire lock. pylint calls it useless-with-lock.
message_templates: '{}()' directly created in 'with' has no effect

title: Unnecessary ellipsis constant.
summary: Used when the ellipsis constant is encountered and can be avoided. A line of code consisting of an ellipsis is unnecessary if there is a docstring on the preceding line or if there is a statement in the same scope. pylint calls it unnecessary-ellipsis.

title: … name "…" contains a non-ASCII character.
summary: Under python 3.5, PEP 3131 allows non-ascii identifiers, but not non-ascii file names.Since Python 3.5, even though Python supports UTF-8 files, some editors or tools don't. pylint calls it non-ascii-file-name.

title: F-strings are not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting.
summary: Used when the py-version set by the user is lower than 3.6 and pylint encounters an f-string. pylint calls it using-f-string-in-unsupported-version.
message_templates: F-strings are not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting

title: Typing.final is not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting.
summary: Used when the py-version set by the user is lower than 3.8 and pylint encounters a typing.final decorator. pylint calls it using-final-decorator-in-unsupported-version.
message_templates: typing.final is not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting

title: Exception groups are not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting.
summary: Used when the py-version set by the user is lower than 3.11 and pylint encounters except* or ExceptionGroup. pylint calls it using-exception-groups-in-unsupported-version.
message_templates: Exception groups are not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting

title: Generic type syntax (PEP 695) is not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting.
summary: Used when the py-version set by the user is lower than 3.12 and pylint encounters generic type syntax. pylint calls it using-generic-type-syntax-in-unsupported-version.
message_templates: Generic type syntax (PEP 695) is not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting

title: Assignment expression is not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting.
summary: Used when the py-version set by the user is lower than 3.8 and pylint encounters an assignment expression (walrus) operator. pylint calls it using-assignment-expression-in-unsupported-version.
message_templates: Assignment expression is not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting

title: Positional-only arguments are not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting.
summary: Used when the py-version set by the user is lower than 3.8 and pylint encounters positional-only arguments. pylint calls it using-positional-only-args-in-unsupported-version.

title: Unpacking in comprehensions is not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting.
summary: Used when the py-version set by the user is lower than 3.15 and pylint encounters the * or ** unpacking added by PEP 798 in a comprehension. pylint calls it using-comprehension-unpacking-in-unsupported-version.
message_templates: Unpacking in comprehensions is not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting

title: Lazy imports are not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting.
summary: Used when the py-version set by the user is lower than 3.15 and pylint encounters the lazy import added by PEP 810. pylint calls it using-lazy-import-in-unsupported-version.
message_templates: Lazy imports are not supported by all versions included in the py-version setting

title: Checks for superfluous trailing whitespace.
summary: According to PEP 8, "avoid trailing whitespace anywhere. Because it’s usually invisible, it can be confusing" Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.253.

title: Checks for files missing a new line at the end of the file.
summary: Trailing blank lines in a file are superfluous. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.61.
message_templates: No newline at end of file

title: Checks for superfluous whitespace in blank lines.
summary: According to PEP 8, "avoid trailing whitespace anywhere. Because it’s usually invisible, it can be confusing" Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.253.
